assumptions: Rule language: terminals nonce, bswap(nonce), midstate words, second-block state after round 2, probe digest words (reduced-round SHA256d of the template at nonce 0) and constants; operations not, bswap, rotr, shr, shl, Sigma0, Sigma1, sigma0, sigma1, xor, and, or, add, sub, Ch, Maj; at most max_size nodes.
Predicate: the expression has j leading zero bits (keeps 2^-j of nonces) or bit b is clear (keeps half).

Hit level: the hash number's top k bits are zero; fitness uses k = fitness_k on the first 2^fitness_bits nonces of each discovery template; held-out tests use all 2^nonce_bits nonces at k = fitness_k and k = 8.
Templates are synthetic (as in the nonce atlas) and every round count cuts all three compressions; reduced-round results say nothing about 64 rounds.
Held-out p-values are one-sided binomial normal approximations with a Bonferroni correction over every held-out test of the run (alpha 0.001).
baseline: A = 1: a selection rule that ignores the hash keeps hits at the overall rate.
conclusion: REDUCED-ROUND ONLY: deviations were detected only for reduced-round variants. These say nothing about full 64-round SHA-256/SHA-256d and give no mining advantage; full-round configurations (where tested) showed no deviation. 4 rounds: 60000 rules evolved; best discovery fitness 1745.7; best held-out amplification at k = 6 is 64.0013 (`keep if bswap((bswap(n) + probe7)) has 6 leading zero bits`); held-out deviation. 5 rounds: 60000 rules evolved; best discovery fitness 3.3; best held-out amplification at k = 6 is 0.9942 (`keep if bit 30 of (not(n) | ch(bswap(n), probe1, ((probe4 + not(n)) << 16))) is 0`); no held-out rule beats A = 1. 6 rounds: 60000 rules evolved; best discovery fitness 3.4; best held-out amplification at k = 6 is 1.0210 (`keep if ((mid2 + n) - ((ch(bswap(n), probe6, n) >> 6) | probe2)) has 6 leading zero bits`); no held-out rule beats A = 1. 8 rounds: 60000 rules evolved; best discovery fitness 4.5; best held-out amplification at k = 6 is 1.0053 (`keep if (((probe5 + mid0) - bswap(mid6)) + (((pre4 >> 4) & 0x7d572cd4) + n)) has 3 leading zero bits`); no held-out rule beats A = 1. 64 rounds: 60000 rules evolved; best discovery fitness 5.0; best held-out amplification at k = 6 is 1.0078 (`keep if maj(bswap(n), maj(smalls0((0x99f1f4d8 | maj(pre5, n, bswap(n)))), (0xa6e0dde7 ^ n), mid4), mid4) has 6 leading zero bits`); no held-out rule beats A = 1. Held-out tests: 100 (rules x hit levels x round counts), Bonferroni threshold 1.0e-5. Work per hit with a rule is 1/A of exhaustive search.

dataset.description: Templates: nonce_atlas::synthetic(seed, i), discovery i < discovery_templates, held-out after; GP randomness SplitMix64::stream(seed ^ rounds, 0).

hypothesis: A cheap expression over the nonce, template constants and a one-hash template probe selects nonces that meet a leading-zero target more often than the rest, on templates the search never saw.
methodology: Per round count: compute the top 16 bits of the hash number for every nonce of each template; evolve a population of rules (tournament selection, subtree crossover and mutation, elitism, parsimony penalty) for a fixed number of generations; keep the best distinct rules; measure each once on the held-out templates.
name: Evolved cheap nonce-selection rules (genetic programming), held-out tested
null_hypothesis: Every evolved rule's held-out amplification is 1 within its confidence interval (at 64 rounds, and at every round count where the header map behaves like a random function).

reproduction.method: full rerun with identical seed and parameters on a separate Rayon pool with a different thread count; SHA-256 of the canonical deterministic results compared

verification.detail: independent hashes and both evaluators agree
verification.method: top 16 hash-number bits recomputed with verification::independent for 256 nonces per round count; vectorised rule evaluation checked against scalar evaluation on 64 random rules per round count
